note: Every case here is implemented by all three packages against fixtures/. A case passing in one package and absent in another is a defect. See runtime-contract.md for the rule each case enforces.

cases.expect: Every row of fixtures/expected-renders.json renders exactly, on every platform

cases.given: A ru message whose variants omit 'many', rendered with count 5
cases.expect: Renders the '*' variant. Does not fail, does not return the key

cases.given: A part object with neither text nor var
cases.expect: That part contributes nothing; the surrounding parts still render
Accepted and applied. auth.sign_out renders 'Выйти'
Accepted
Accepted. The added key settings.title is present in the catalog and has no accessor
Refused. Previous catalog stays. onDiagnostic called naming the policy

cases.rule: contract §5 — holds under every policy including a range
cases.expect: Refused under none, patchOnly, minorAndPatch and any range. Nothing written
No request is made at all, not merely a refused result
Refused. Downgrade is not an update

upToDate, not refusedByPolicy. Nothing was refused — the server and the app agree. Calling it a refusal sends whoever is debugging to the wrong setting, and this is the most common outcome in production
Accepted. Versions compare numerically, not as strings
Refused, reported, no throw

cases.rule: contract §4 — the case the current implementation gets wrong
cases.expect: Refused. The version is a patch and passes policy, but inbox.unread retyped count from NUMBER to STRING. Checking names alone accepts it; that is the bug this case exists to catch
Refused whole. No key from that catalog is applied
Accepted. An added key is not a client failure

cases.rule: contract §4 — the signature is a floor, not an equality
cases.given: A present key declaring an extra parameter the signature does not name
cases.expect: Accepted

cases.given: A catalog where one key of four is incompatible
cases.expect: None of the four applied. Not three

cases.given: A cached catalog from before the app upgraded, and a new signature
cases.expect: Checked again on load, and dropped if it no longer satisfies the new signature

cases.rule: contract §6 — not done by the current implementation
cases.given: An ETag held from a previous fetch
cases.expect: If-None-Match carries it on the next request
Current catalog untouched. Reported as success, not failure
X-Localaze-Key carries the configured key. The project and environment appear in no parameter

cases.rule: contract §6, §8 — found by the example app, not by a unit test
cases.expect: The diagnostic names the 401. A wrong API key must be distinguishable from a quiet network, and reporting only "the published version could not be read" makes the two identical
version=x.y.z on the request, and the pinned release is what arrives

cases.given: A downloaded catalog that fails the signature check
cases.expect: The cache is not touched. Order is policy, version, download, signature, persist

cases.given: All four levels present with different text for one key
cases.expect: Applied wins, then cached, then bundled, then compiled-in

cases.rule: contract §7 — per key, not per catalog
cases.expect: billing.due falls through to the compiled-in copy while the other three come from the asset

cases.given: A catalog applied and persisted, then a fresh start
cases.expect: The persisted catalog is used ahead of the bundled copy
An applied update works for the session and is gone on restart. Not an error

cases.rule: LZ-58 — works fully offline on first launch
cases.given: Fresh install, no network, no cache
cases.expect: Every key renders from the bundled asset with no request made
Returns, does not throw. Current content kept. onDiagnostic called
Returns, does not throw. Current content kept
Returns, does not throw. The status appears in the diagnostic, because a 401 is a wrong key and must be distinguishable from a quiet network
Returns, does not throw. Current content kept
Returns, does not throw. Current content kept

cases.given: An unreadable or truncated cache file
cases.expect: Ignored, falls through to bundled. Reported, not thrown

cases.rule: contract §8 — why the compiled-in copy exists
cases.expect: Every key renders from the compiled-in copy. A path typo is stale text, never a blank screen

cases.given: The cache directory cannot be written
cases.expect: The update applies for this session and is reported as not persisted. Not an error
Swallowed. A broken diagnostic must not take the app with it

cases.rule: contract §8 — the rule the whole group serves
cases.given: Every failure above, exercised against every public method
cases.expect: Not one throws, returns a failed future, or propagates
Last-fetch status is readable, so an app can report it rather than guess
Every other option takes its documented default and the SDK behaves sensibly

cases.given: A catalog accepted mid-session, default config
cases.expect: Rendering is unchanged until next launch. Text changing under a user mid-session is worse than being a launch out of date
The version currently rendering is readable, so an app can report it
No MF2 parsing, no '.match', no '.input', no '{{'. A device never sees MF2 syntax
No CLDR tables. Plural categories resolve through rules the generator compiled in
No key names, no translated text, no project identifier. The packages are generic
No direct network or filesystem call. Transport and storage arrive as injected interfaces
Output is byte-identical to the package's checked-in golden file

cases.given: The golden output compiled against the package
cases.expect: Every row of fixtures/expected-renders.json renders exactly
--assets holds one <language>.json per manifest language, byte-identical to its input catalog
authSignOut is a property; authWelcome takes a string; billingDue a date; inboxUnread a number and passes it as the selector

cases.expect: Exits non-zero naming the language. Nothing written

cases.expect: Exits non-zero naming the key and language. Nothing written
Generates. The gap is reported, not fatal

cases.expect: Exits non-zero naming both versions. Nothing written

cases.expect: Every problem is printed, not only the first
